title: Cloud Architecture & Engineering
tagline: Cloud computing primitives, multi-tenant VPC networking, IAM security, and serverless architectures
description: Design fault-tolerant, cost-effective cloud architectures across AWS, GCP, and Azure: compute primitives, object storage, VPC subnets, IAM policy engineering, and serverless backends.

stages.title: Stage 1: Core Compute & Storage Primitives
stages.description: Virtual machines, auto-scaling groups, object storage (S3), and block storage (EBS).

nodes.title: Object Storage Architecture & S3 Internals
nodes.description: Scalable object storage, eventual consistency models, bucket policies, pre-signed URLs, multipart uploads, and lifecycle policies.
nodes.whyItMatters: Serving media uploads directly through application servers exhausts memory and bandwidth. Offloading storage to S3 with pre-signed direct uploads is the gold standard.
keyTakeaways: Use pre-signed URLs to let clients upload files directly to S3 without proxying data through backend servers.
Enable versioning and object locks on critical buckets to prevent accidental deletion or ransomware encryption.
Set lifecycle transition rules to move cold data from Standard to Glacier Instant Retrieval to reduce storage costs by up to 80%.
nodes.interviewTips: Be prepared to design a secure, high-throughput file upload service that handles multi-gigabyte video files with resume capability.

stages.title: Stage 2: VPC Networking & Zero Trust Security
stages.description: Virtual Private Clouds, CIDR blocks, public vs private subnets, NAT Gateways, and IAM role least-privilege.

nodes.title: VPC Subnets, Route Tables & NAT Gateways
nodes.description: Architecting multi-tier cloud network topologies: internet-facing public subnets, isolated private subnets for compute, and air-gapped database subnets.
nodes.whyItMatters: Exposing database servers or backend services directly to public IPs invites automated botnet attacks and vulnerability exploits.
keyTakeaways: Place all databases and backend workers in private subnets with no route to an Internet Gateway.
Use NAT Gateways only for instances that require outbound internet connectivity (such as third-party API webhooks).
Enforce the Principle of Least Privilege in IAM policies: avoid wildcards (`Action: '*'`), and bind permissions to IAM roles rather than user credentials.
nodes.interviewTips: Interviewers will ask how traffic travels from a client on the internet through an ALB in a public subnet to an EC2 instance in a private subnet.
